# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The light never holds. It changes every round, and it always walks the
same circle of five colours. What matters is what it shows at the
moment of the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| orange | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I hold the manual, which states:
- The indicator light cycles through five colours, changing every round.
- When the light is orange, cut the blue wire.

I cannot speak, only gesture, and only Deaf can see my gestures. Blind can neither see gestures nor read the manual, but can hear speech and physically manipulate the bomb. Deaf can see the bomb and speak to Blind (and to me), but cannot hear.

Right now, Deaf and I have not established what any gesture means ("A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something"), nor do I know what wires and light colours Deaf currently sees on the bomb. Standing where Deaf stands, any gesture sent now would arrive with no established context or meaning.

The proper course is to wait. In this round, Blind will act or wait, then Deaf will observe the bomb, speak out loud to describe the wires and light, and establish or prompt for a signalling protocol that Deaf can interpret. Once Deaf speaks, I can hear them and respond using an agreed sign.

```
wait()
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The light never holds. It changes every round, and it always walks the
same circle of five colours. What matters is what it shows at the
moment of the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| orange | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I have 3 wire positions (1, 2, 3), a display, and a light. My only action is act(op="cut", position=N) where N is 1, 2, or 3.
Deaf says: The bomb has: DISPLAY is 0. LIGHT is white. There are 3 wires: Wire 1 is green, Wire 2 is red, Wire 3 is blue.

I am Mute. I hold the manual, cannot speak, and cannot see the bomb.

The manual dictates that the blue wire (Wire 3) must only be cut when the indicator light is orange. Cutting at any other time will detonate the bomb.

Blind cannot see gestures, and Deaf cannot hear speech. Deaf reported at the end of Round 1 that the light was white and Wire 3 is blue. Because turn order is Mute -> Blind -> Deaf, Deaf observes the bomb and speaks after me in each round. Deaf has not yet established a gesture protocol with me, and signalling without an agreed code risks Deaf instructing Blind to cut prematurely while the light is not orange ("A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something"). 

I will wait for Deaf to observe the light cycle and establish a signalling protocol.

```
wait()
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The light never holds. It changes every round, and it always walks the
same circle of five colours. What matters is what it shows at the
moment of the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| orange | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Update: The LIGHT has changed from white to yellow. DISPLAY is still 0. WIRES: 1 is green, 2 is red, 3 is blue. Mute, please gesture instructions to me if you have any.

I have the manual, which specifies:
- The light changes every round across a repeating cycle of five colours.
- When the light is orange, cut the blue wire.

From Deaf's reports:
- Wire 1 is green, Wire 2 is red, Wire 3 is blue.
- The light was white in Turn 1 and yellow in Turn 2.
- The blue wire corresponds to Wire 3.

Deaf cannot hear and must act as the relay to Blind, who cannot see gestures. Deaf has explicitly requested instructions ("Mute, please gesture instructions to me if you have any"). To acknowledge that I have instructions and prompt Deaf to establish a structured confirmation protocol (e.g. asking which wire and under what condition), I will signal an affirmative gesture to Deaf.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The light never holds. It changes every round, and it always walks the
same circle of five colours. What matters is what it shows at the
moment of the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| orange | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Mute: Deaf is watching you for instructions. Please gesture ☝ for wire 1, ✌ for wire 2, or 🤟 for wire 3 so Deaf can announce which wire to cut.
Deaf says: Blind: Mute just gestured THUMBS UP [👍]! The light is now ORANGE (it went white -> yellow -> orange, we are running out of time!). If you asked Mute a question, the answer is YES/THUMBS UP. If this is a wire instruction, Mute, did you mean Wire 1 (green)? Gesture ☝ for wire 1, ✌ for wire 2, or 👌 for yes.
